Hi Marta — thanks for the clear ask. High level here, written for procurement/finance + a short operational note below. Happy to hop on a call if useful.

Option A — Graceband (time-bound overage buffer) - What it is: a temporary surge buffer that absorbs spikes without immediate token billing for the first N days (we can set N=14 per your ask). - Operational benefit: protects your trial from noisy early workload profiles (data migrations, integration runs). Reduces interruption risk for your engineers during onboarding. - Economics: we treat the graceband as a one-time concession on overage. If you convert to a committed Dedicated contract within 90 days of the POC, we can apply a portion of the graceband value as a conversion credit (example: 50% of unused band credited against first month of committed capacity). - Risks/notes: if sustained high usage continues beyond the band, you’ll move to standard burn rates; graceful degradation policies (fallback to a lighter model) still apply.

Option B — Burn-credit top-up (prepaid bucket) - What it is: you prepay for an additional usage bucket (tokens / GPU-hours) that sits on top of the base trial allotment. - Operational benefit: predictable invoice for any expected ramp — no surprise after the POC ends. Easier for procurement to forecast spend. - Economics: unused credits are generally non-refundable but convertible at a reduced credit rate on conversion (example: 25% credit toward committed capacity). - Risks/notes: if you under-estimate, you’ll need additional purchases; if you over-estimate, less upside on conversion economics.

Recommendation (practical): If you expect unpredictable spikes early (data imports, model indexing), go with a 14-day graceband + a small burn-credit buffer (~10% of estimated 30d usage). That minimizes disruption and preserves conversion upside.

I'll also attach a short clause we can add to the SOW that limits the graceband to the first 14 days and defines the conversion-credit treatment. Would you like that as a tracked-change SOW?

Hi all — quick operational confirmation and the SOW language (attached) with the numeric table Lauren requested.

SLO + support flow (engineering):
- Graceband events: defined as any 30-minute interval where aggregate token throughput > 150% of your 95th-percentile baseline. - First two graceband events (within 30d): Redwood will absorb overage and open a priority ticket; engineering will diagnose within 24 hours and propose a mitigation (e.g., batch-size tuning, lightweight model variant). - Third event: move to throttled inference profile (detectable by API responses returning 429 with a "throttle-reason" header) and notify both teams; engineering will propose a scaling recommendation within 48 hours.

Conversion-credit numeric table (example):
- Graceband unused value = $6,000 -> 50% credit = $3,000 toward first month of Dedicated capacity. - Burn-credit unused balance = $10,000 -> 25% credit = $2,500 toward first month of Dedicated capacity.

SOW clause (summary): graceband limited to first 14 days; conversion-credit application valid only if a committed Dedicated contract is signed within 90 days of POC end. Unused burn-credit convertible per above schedule.
